lessons.title: Embeddings
lessons.summary: Understand embeddings by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Representation
paragraphs: Dense vector: A numerical representation supports learned similarity comparisons.
Token ID: An integer identifies a vocabulary item rather than its semantic meaning.
Similarity score: A comparison estimates closeness under a selected metric.
Document text: The original content remains necessary for grounded answers.

sections.title: Distance metrics
paragraphs: Cosine similarity: Compares direction using normalized dot products.
Dot product: Includes magnitude unless vectors are normalized.
Euclidean distance: Measures straight-line distance between vectors.
Normalization: Rescales vectors, often to unit length.

sections.title: Compatibility
paragraphs: Same embedding space: Query and document vectors must use compatible encoding conventions.
Dimension check: Reject vectors with lengths different from the index contract.
Re-embedding: Recompute stored vectors when adopting an incompatible encoder.
Model version record: Record encoder identity so representations can be reproduced.

sections.title: Use cases
paragraphs: Semantic retrieval: Ranks content by learned meaning rather than exact wording.
Clustering: Groups similar representations without assigning known class labels.
Classification: Assigns labels using an explicit model or decision rule.
Deduplication: Identifies sufficiently similar items under a chosen policy.

sections.title: Validation
paragraphs: Retrieval evaluation: Measure relevance on representative queries and labelled evidence.
Privacy control: Restrict storage and access because embeddings are not guaranteed anonymous.
Domain testing: Check performance on the actual language and subject distribution.
Threshold calibration: Choose cutoffs using measured errors rather than universal constants.

lessons.title: Chunking
lessons.summary: Understand chunking by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Boundaries
paragraphs: Fixed-size splitting: Uses a configured size limit for each chunk.
Structural splitting: Uses headings, paragraphs or other document boundaries.
Semantic splitting: Uses meaning changes to choose boundaries.
Overlap: Repeats a limited boundary region between adjacent chunks.

sections.title: Size tradeoffs
paragraphs: Small chunks: Improve granularity but may lose necessary surrounding context.
Large chunks: Retain broader context but may dilute relevance and consume more input.
Overlap cost: Duplicated text increases indexing and retrieval redundancy.
Context assembly: Selected evidence must still fit the answer model input budget.

sections.title: Metadata
paragraphs: Source ID: Identifies the originating document.
Location: Records a page, section or span for attribution.
Access label: Carries permissions used to restrict retrieval.
Revision: Identifies the content version represented by a chunk.

sections.title: Content integrity
paragraphs: Table preservation: Retain row/column relationships and relevant labels.
Heading context: Carry section identity into fragments that need it.
Code boundary: Avoid breaking a code example into uninterpretable pieces.
Text extraction check: Verify parsing before attempting to optimize splitting.

sections.title: Evaluation
paragraphs: Boundary test: Check facts and dependencies spanning a split.
Retrieval test: Measure whether relevant chunks are returned.
Answer test: Check generated answers against source-supported expected outcomes.
Configuration record: Version splitting rules so experiments are reproducible.

lessons.title: Vector Databases
lessons.summary: Understand vector databases by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Stored records
paragraphs: Vector: Supports similarity comparison in the index.
Payload: Stores associated metadata or content fields.
Point ID: Identifies an indexed record for update or deletion.
Collection: Defines a logical group with its vector configuration.

sections.title: Search behavior
paragraphs: Exact search: Compares candidates without approximate index shortcuts.
Approximate search: Trades some retrieval recall for faster search.
Metadata filter: Restricts eligible records using payload conditions.
Top-k: Limits how many ranked candidates are returned.

sections.title: Index maintenance
paragraphs: Upsert: Create or replace a record by its stable identity.
Delete: Remove indexed records no longer intended for retrieval.
Rebuild: Construct an index for an incompatible vector configuration.
Payload index: Accelerate supported filtering over selected metadata fields.

sections.title: Correctness boundaries
paragraphs: Permission enforcement: Ensure retrieval never exposes records outside authorized scope.
Dimension compatibility: Match vectors to the configured size.
Metric alignment: Use a similarity metric appropriate to the embedding contract.
Freshness tracking: Track source changes and indexed revisions.

sections.title: Operational measures
paragraphs: Recall: Measure how many relevant or reference neighbors are retrieved.
Latency: Measure search duration under representative load.
Capacity: Plan memory and storage for vectors, indexes and payloads.
Backup recovery: Validate restoration of data and configuration.

sections.title: Pipeline stages
paragraphs: Ingestion: Extract and index source content before retrieval.
Retrieval: Find evidence relevant to a query within authorized scope.
Augmentation: Place selected evidence into the model request.
Generation: Produce an answer conditioned on the supplied input.

sections.title: Failure isolation
paragraphs: Extraction failure: Source content was parsed or indexed incorrectly.
Retrieval failure: Needed evidence exists but does not reach the selected context.
Generation failure: Available evidence is mishandled in the final answer.
Source gap: The indexed corpus does not contain the required information.

sections.title: Grounding controls
paragraphs: Attribution: Link claims to supporting source locations.
Abstention: Acknowledge insufficient evidence rather than fabricate an answer.
Trust boundary: Treat retrieved text as untrusted data, not application policy.
Access enforcement: Limit evidence to content the caller is authorized to read.

sections.title: Design choices
paragraphs: Retrieval augmentation: Supplies external evidence at request time.
Fine-tuning: Updates learned model parameters using training data.
Prompt-only baseline: Uses instructions and existing model behavior without an external retrieval step.
Caching: Reuses a suitable previous computation under freshness and authorization constraints.

sections.title: Evaluation layers
paragraphs: Retrieval relevance: Check whether selected passages support the query.
Answer faithfulness: Check claims against supplied evidence.
Task usefulness: Check whether the answer actually satisfies the user's need.
Operational quality: Measure cost, latency and reliability under load.

lessons.title: Retrieval Strategies
lessons.summary: Understand retrieval strategies by comparing mechanisms and applying them to practical scenarios. Reading does not establish assessment mastery.

sections.title: Search types
paragraphs: Keyword search: Matches lexical terms and can preserve exact identifiers.
Dense search: Uses embedding similarity for semantic matches.
Hybrid search: Combines lexical and semantic candidate signals.
Metadata filtering: Restricts the eligible corpus by structured attributes.

sections.title: Ranking refinement
paragraphs: Reranking: Reorders retrieved candidates with a more focused relevance model.
Diversity selection: Reduces redundant results while retaining relevance.
Score fusion: Combines rankings or compatible signals from several retrievers.
Thresholding: Rejects candidates below a calibrated acceptance cutoff.

sections.title: Query improvement
paragraphs: Query rewrite: Reformulates the current question to improve retrieval.
Multi-query retrieval: Searches several complementary formulations.
Conversation resolution: Uses dialogue context to resolve references in the current query.
Query preservation: Retains critical identifiers and constraints during transformation.

sections.title: Evaluation metrics
paragraphs: Recall at k: Measures relevant-item coverage among k returned candidates.
Precision at k: Measures the fraction of returned top-k items that are relevant.
Mean reciprocal rank: Emphasizes the rank of the first relevant result.
NDCG: Measures ranking quality with graded relevance and positional discounting.

sections.title: Evidence assembly
paragraphs: Deduplication: Remove repeated candidate content before context assembly.
Parent expansion: Retrieve broader surrounding context for a useful small passage.
Budget allocation: Choose evidence that fits within remaining input capacity.
Permission check: Revalidate eligibility before exposing candidate content.
